title: Opening the character creator
summary: cc.open opens the creator from normal play by Character Customization Anywhere's route (the pause menu redirected to the mirror's scenario), after taking the save lock; cc.page points the creator's camera at a part of V.
limits: Refused in combat, a scene (tier 3 and above; V's apartment, tier 2, is accepted), a vehicle, a menu, a Johnny section or where photo mode isn't allowed; only with allow_creator_leave (the -writes build).
quirks: A request withdrawn after its event may still let the pause menu open (pause_menu_may_open).
notes: cc.open and cc.back from the street were seen working in sessions 4 to 6.

title: Changing creator options
summary: cc.apply changes one creator option through the option's own row, by name, on-screen label or slot, with the value by index, name or label; it never confirms.
quirks: Options are matched by name or label, never a stored index (ArchiveXL rebuilds indices); a value already shown is a no-op success.

title: Confirm and Back in the creator
summary: cc.confirm keeps the look and cc.back discards it, through the creator's own functions; cc.confirm never discards a change.
limits: Only with allow_creator_leave = true, in sessions that end by loading the safety save (the maintainer's decision of 26 September).

title: V's clothing inventory
summary: inventory.list reads the clothing V owns, one entry per copy; inventory.equip and inventory.unequip equip by record (optionally adding it) or empty a slot, each waiting for the slot and answering its undo.
limits: Clothing slots only, in normal play outside combat and scene tiers 3-5; writes off until the maintainer approves the inventory class (the test zip adds it with --allow-inventory).
quirks: An active wardrobe outfit can keep an equipped item from drawing (hidden_by_outfit); sessions 4 and 5's helmet was equipped but hidden.

title: Cyberware
summary: cyberware.state reads V's cyberware area by area with the arms' holster chain and humanity; cyberware.equip and cyberware.unequip use the ripperdoc's own requests, holstering the arms first.
notes: Ran in session 8's checks (the render study's arm captures).

title: Live posing (L0)
summary: pose.live.read checks a loaded XF carrier clip against the layout the bridge expects; pose.live.apply writes joint rotations into its constant keys in photo mode, with the carrier's own keys kept for the undo and the kill switch.

demand.note: Live posing through the bridge: pose V from the Studio and see it in the running game.

limits: Only with allow_live_pose (the -writes build) and the separate XF Live Pose test package; refused for the session when an engine address is missing (live_pose_unavailable).
